items: MPPT charge controller (or one built into an all-in-one inverter)
LiFePO4 battery bank at the inverter's nominal voltage (e.g. 48 V)
off-grid pure sine wave inverter (120/240 V split-phase for full-time cabins)
alternative for weekend cabins: an expandable power station plus matched portable panels
cart: One store per kit: bluettipower.com (weekend kit, e.g. Elite 200 V2 + 2× 200 W, or Apex 300 + SORA 500), iallpowers.com (medium kit, R4000 + SP037 panels), sungoldpower.com (full-time kit, SGR-8K10E complete 8 kW / 10.24 kWh / 3.6 kW panels)
why: Both of ChatGPT's answers present the cabin as a system of panels, MPPT controller, LiFePO4 battery, inverter and protection, sized in three tiers from weekend (400–1,500 W of panels, 2–5 kWh) to full-time (4–8 kW, 10–30 kWh), and it showed no catalog card for any complete set. The deciding facts are that battery voltage must match the inverter and charge controller (48 V class), and that the PV input limit and winter solar yield set the array size, so a weekend cabin is best served by a plug-and-play power station with matched panels while a full-time cabin needs a 120/240 V split-phase inverter kit, and each of these can be bought in a single brand's cart.
